name: Neuroendocrine Tumor with Other Location

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of neuroendocrine differentiation by immunohistochemistry (chromogranin A, synaptophysin positivity)
Identification of tumor location and extent by cross-sectional imaging (CT, MRI) or functional imaging (68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT)
Elevated serum or urine markers such as chromogranin A or 5-HIAA depending on tumor secretory status

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus imaging evidence of tumor location
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of primary pancreatic or pulmonary NET to confirm other location

pathognomonic.symptomName: Flushing episodes due to carcinoid syndrome
Secretory diarrhea associated with hormone secretion
pathognomonic.notes: Common in functional NETs producing vasoactive substances

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain localized to tumor site
common.notes: Often due to mass effect or local invasion

searchTerms: low energy from ongoing health issues

common.notes: Depends on tumor size and location

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral edema due to carcinoid heart disease
searchTerms: fluid buildup in legs from heart valve damage
peripheral edema due to heart tumor effects

occasional.symptomName: Hypoglycemia from insulin secretion in functional tumors
occasional.notes: Rare in non-pancreatic NETs but possible
searchTerms: low blood sugar from insulin tumor
neurological signs due to paraneoplastic effects
brain or nerve problems from tumor

rare.symptomName: Cushingoid features due to ectopic ACTH secretion
searchTerms: symptoms of high cortisol due to ectopic hormone
signs of cortisol excess from tumor hormone
low blood pressure from vasoactive peptides

laboratory: Hormone assays depending on secretory profile (e.g., insulin, ACTH)
imaging: CT or MRI showing mass in atypical neuroendocrine tumor location
Echocardiography for carcinoid heart disease assessment
genetic: Somatic mutations in MEN1, DAXX, ATRX genes in some cases
No consistent germline mutation unless associated with hereditary syndromes
other: Histopathology with immunohistochemical staining positive for synaptophysin and chromogranin A
Ki-67 proliferation index for grading tumor aggressiveness

distinguishingFeatures: Distinct imaging findings localized to pancreas
High mitotic rate and necrosis on histology

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mass with local invasion
Signs of carcinoid heart disease (e.g., right heart failure)
Severe secretory diarrhea causing dehydration and electrolyte imbalance
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of Endocrine Organs, 4th Edition, 2017
Orphanet: Neuroendocrine Tumor with Other Location (ORPHA:100101)
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Neuroendocrine Tumors, 2024
